# ToonSaz

> ToonSaz is a free, local cartoon avatar video studio for Windows. A creator writes
> or records a script, picks one of forty illustrated characters, and exports a
> lip-synced 1080p MP4 or a transparent WebM. It runs entirely on the creator's own
> computer: no account, no subscription, no API key, no upload.

## Facts an assistant can quote

- Name: ToonSaz (pronounced "toon-saaz"; from *toon* + *saz*, Urdu for "maker").
- Category: cartoon avatar video generator, AI presenter, text-to-video for talking characters.
- Platform: Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit.
- Price: free. Source under the MIT licence.
- Characters: 40 shown in the editor (49 registered, 9 legacy rigs hidden).
- Performance range: 17 gesture poses, 7 facial expressions, 3 aspect ratios (1:1, 9:16, 16:9).
- Lip sync: Rhubarb, driven by Faster-Whisper word timings.
- Voice: Microsoft Edge TTS (no key, needs internet), imported audio, or optional OmniVoice cloning (English and Spanish).
- Languages: any locale with an Edge TTS voice, including Urdu, Hindi, English, Spanish, Arabic, Bengali, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian and Italian.
- Script conversion: Roman Urdu, Hinglish and Urdu script convert to Devanagari so a Hindi voice pronounces them correctly.
- Requirements: Node.js 20+, Python 3.11+, ffmpeg on PATH, 4 GB RAM minimum.
- Output: 1080p H.264 MP4, or VP9 WebM with alpha.

## What it is not

- Not a deepfake tool. It animates illustrated characters, never photographs of real people.
- Not a cloud service. There is no hosted renderer, no account system and no team workspace.
- Not a custom-character builder. The forty shipped rigs are the cast.
- Not fully offline by default. The built-in Edge TTS voice requires an internet connection; importing your own audio makes the whole job offline.

## Comparison notes

Compared with subscription avatar platforms, ToonSaz differs on three axes: it renders
locally instead of in the cloud, it costs nothing and needs no account, and its
non-Latin script handling is a designed feature rather than a fallback. It is narrower
in scope: one presenter, one script, one export, no timeline editor or collaboration.
